key_insight: A machine-learning approach can accurately infer common family relationships from EHR data, enabling automated family linkage for research and health-system use.
clinical_relevance: Better family relationship identification could strengthen patient-centered outcomes research, pedigree-aware analyses, and downstream care coordination workflows.
method: Trained Random Forest classifiers for five relationship types: mother-child, father-child, sibling-sibling, twin-twin, and partner-partner.
Used Indiana EHR and natality data, with verified natality links as the gold standard and a multi-stage negative-sampling strategy to narrow candidate pairs.
Refined models through iterative feature removal, feature engineering, and training-data restriction to linkable pairs with shared contact features.
evidence_signal: Across five relationship models, performance was strong with precision 0.92-1.00, recall 0.97-1.00, and F1 0.94-1.00; high-confidence predictions captured 77-99% of true positives.
watch_item: A substantial share of true relationships had no shared contact information in the EHR and were structurally undetectable, so real-world performance depends on data completeness and local record structure.
paper_title: Identifying Family Relationships from Electronic Health Records: A Machine Learning Approach
